```{r, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE} library(tidyverse) library(flextable) library(ggpubr) library(kableExtra) ```
#### Load the mpg dataset ```{r} data(iris) ```
Every row in mpg is a car, every column a feature of that car. mpg stands for miles per gallon. ```{r} head(iris) ``` ## Standard themes The default theme, featuring a gray background and white gridlines. ### theme_gray ```{r} plot <- ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = Species)) + geom_point() plot + theme_gray() ```
### theme_bw A black on white theme. ```{r} plot + theme_bw() ```
### theme_linedraw A theme with only black lines of various widths on white backgrounds. ```{r} plot + theme_linedraw() ```
### theme_light A theme similar to theme_linedraw but with grey lines and axes designed to draw more attention to the data. ```{r} plot + theme_light() ```
### theme_dark A theme similar to theme_light, but with a dark background. A useful theme for making thin colored lines stand out. ```{r} plot + theme_dark() ```
### theme_minimal A theme with no background annotations. ```{r} plot + theme_minimal() ```
### theme_classic A theme with no gridlines. ```{r} plot + theme_classic() ```
### theme_void A completely empty theme. ```{r} plot + theme_void() ```
## ggthemes library Next, we’ll show a few examples of how to use the predefined themes to modify the aesthetics of plots. ```{r} library(ggthemes) ```
### theme_wsj The Wall Street Journal's theme. ```{r} plot + theme_wsj() ```
### theme_tufte A minimalist theme inspired by the work of statistician Edward Tufte. ```{r} plot + theme_tufte() ```
### theme_solarized A theme that uses colors based on the solarized palette. ```{r} plot + theme_solarized() ```
```{r} plot + theme_solarized(light = FALSE) ```
### theme_gdocs A theme with Google Docs Chart defaults. ```{r} plot + theme_gdocs() ```
### theme_fivethirtyeight Theme inspired by fivethirtyeight.com plots. ```{r} plot + theme_fivethirtyeight() ```
### theme_economist Theme inspired by The Economist. ```{r} plot + theme_economist() ```
## Sources [ggplot2 themes](https://www.statology.org/best-ggplot2-themes/)
